mainTopic: The razor in a נזיר's shaving, how much hair counts for each law, and how we learn that a מצורע must shave with a razor
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא. We cannot learn a נזיר's razor rule from a מצורע, because we do not learn from a strict case to make a lighter case stricter. רבי learns from 'until the completion' that the final shaving must be done with a razor, and the word 'razor' in the איסור adds a second לאו. רב חסדא then gives three amounts: one hair for מלקות, two leftover hairs to invalidate the final shaving, and most of the head 'like a razor' to cancel days. רבי שמעון holds that two hairs are enough to cancel days. Next, a משנה teaches that a נזיר, a מצורע and the לויים must shave as a מצוה, with a razor and leaving no two hairs, so a hair-removing paste does not count. The גמרא looks for a source that a מצורע needs a razor and builds a הצד השוה from the לויים and the נזיר. רבא מברניש begins to challenge that proof, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the razor rule cannot be learned from a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its reasoning: we cannot learn the נזיר's razor rule from the מצורע, because we do not learn from a strict case to make a lighter case stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do not learn a lighter case from a stricter case in order to make the lighter case stricter.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a reason that started before this part of the daf. It explains why the תורה had to say clearly that a נזיר shaves with a תער.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע is the stricter case, since he must shave his whole body. A rule found only by a מצורע cannot be carried over to make a נזיר stricter. So the תורה had to state the razor rule for a נזיר on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: we learn or derive (one law from another)
the lighter, less strict case
the stricter, more serious case
to make a law stricter

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a קל וחומר. A קל וחומר goes from light to strict. This rule says the opposite direction is not allowed: you cannot take a rule that exists only in the strict case and use it to tighten up the light case.

phrases.english: as we do not derive a lenient case from a stringent one
phrases.notes: The lighter case here is the נזיר and the stricter case is the מצורע, who has to shave his whole body.

phrases.english: to be stringent upon it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין דָּנִין קַל מֵחָמוּר לְהַחְמִיר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's reasoning from the earlier part of the daf about why the word תער is needed for a נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You cannot take a rule from the stricter case of a מצורע to make the lighter case of a נזיר stricter. So the razor rule for a נזיר needs its own source.

steps.title: רבי learns the razor rule from 'until the completion'
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the word תער is not needed for this rule. The פסוק 'a razor shall not come upon his head until the completion' already shows that after the term ends, the shaving is done only with a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: it is not needed, because the פסוק says, 'A razor shall not come upon his head until the completion.' The תורה is saying: after the completion, the shaving may be done only with a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי offers a different source for the rule that a נזיר's final shaving must be with a תער.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads the פסוק as one sentence: no razor until the term is complete. That suggests that once the term is complete, a razor is used. So the תגלחת at the end must be done with a razor, and no separate word is needed to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not needed
a razor
the completion (of the נזירות term)
the shaving (here, the נזיר's shaving at the end of his term)

phrases.english: Rabbi says: It is not necessary,
phrases.notes: He means the separate word 'razor' is not needed to teach that the final shaving uses a razor.

phrases.english: for it says:
"A razor shall not come upon his head
until the completion";
the Torah is saying: "After the completion"
phrases.notes: These words are not in the פסוק. רבי is explaining what 'until the completion' implies.

phrases.english: the shaving shall be only with a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source from the ברייתא's first opinion for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'until the completion' we learn that after the term ends, the shaving must be done only with a razor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading leads straight into the next question: if 'razor' in this פסוק really means a razor, what does it mean in the איסור of shaving?

steps.title: But the איסור of shaving also mentions a razor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the first half of the פסוק says 'a razor shall not come upon his head,' yet a נזיר may not remove hair in any way. So why does it mention a razor?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'A razor shall not come upon his head'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading. The same words that mention a razor also make up the איסור of shaving, and that איסור is not only about razors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read 'razor' strictly, the איסור would cover only a razor. But it is accepted that a נזיר may not remove his hair by any method. So the word 'razor' in this איסור needs its own explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is written (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
shall not come upon / pass over
his head

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "A razor shall not come upon his head"!
phrases.notes: The point: a נזיר may not remove hair in any way, so why does this איסור single out a razor?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב תַּעַר לֹא יַעֲבוֹר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the word תער in the same פסוק is understood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of תער in the איסור of shaving for a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איסור applies to removing hair in any way, so naming a razor seems to add nothing, or even to wrongly limit the איסור.

steps.title: The razor brings a second לאו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'razor' teaches that someone who shaves with a razor breaks two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to make him break two לאוין for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the איסור mentions a razor even though any hair removal is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Shall not come upon his head' already forbids removing hair in any way. The word 'razor' adds a second לאו for using a razor. So a נזיר who shaves with a razor breaks two לאוין.

keyTerms.meaning: to make him break (an איסור) for it
two
negative commandments (plural of לאו)

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר may not remove his hair in any way. If he shaves with a razor, he breaks two לאוין. רבי learns from 'until the completion' that the final shaving must be done with a razor.

phrases.english: To make him violate two prohibitions for it.
phrases.notes: One לאו is for removing hair at all, and the second is for doing it with a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word its own job: an extra לאו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of a razor seemed pointless, since any hair removal is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'razor' adds a second לאו for shaving with a razor, so that act breaks two לאוין.

steps.title: Three laws, three different amounts of hair
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules: one hair is enough for מלקות, leaving two hairs ruins the final shaving, and only shaving most of the head with a razor cancels the נזיר's days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: for lashes, one hair is enough. To hold back the final shaving, two hairs left over are enough. To cancel his days, he only cancels them if he shaves most of his head, and with a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives three separate rules about a נזיר and his hair, each with its own amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing even one hair is a forbidden act, so it earns מלקות. At the end of the term, the shaving counts only if almost every hair is gone, so two leftover hairs hold it back. Cancelling days already counted (סתירה) needs much more: most of the head, shaved with a razor.

keyTerms.meaning: to receive lashes (מלקות) as punishment
to hold back or invalidate, so the act does not count
to cancel the days of נזירות already counted
most of his head

steps.confusionAlert: These are three different laws with three different amounts. Do not mix them up: one hair for lashes, two hairs left over for the final shaving, most of the head for cancelling days.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section of the sugya is built on these three amounts, and especially on the words 'with a razor.'

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
For lashes — with one [hair];
to hold back — with two;
phrases.notes: This is about the shaving at the end of the term. If two hairs are left, that shaving does not count.

phrases.english: to cancel — he does not cancel [his days]
except with most of his head, and with a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the amounts of hair for each law of a נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One hair is enough for מלקות. Two leftover hairs invalidate the final shaving. Cancelling days requires most of the head, shaved with a razor.

steps.title: But every tool that removes hair is included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רב חסדא mean that only a razor counts? A ברייתא includes every tool that removes hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a razor, yes, but with something else, no? But it was taught: 'From where do we know to include every tool that removes hair?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's words 'with a razor' by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רב חסדא seems to say that days are cancelled only when a razor is used. But the ברייתא learns that every tool that removes hair counts for a נזיר. If every tool counts, why should only a razor cancel the days?

keyTerms.meaning: something else, another thing
but it is taught (in a ברייתא)
things that remove (hair)

phrases.english: With a razor — yes,
with something else — no?
But it is taught:
From where do we include all things that remove [hair]!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתַעַר אִין בְּמִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא לָא וְהָקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the words 'with a razor' in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא includes every tool that removes hair, so limiting the rule to a razor goes against it.

steps.title: Read it as 'like a razor'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רב חסדא's wording: he meant 'in the manner of a razor,' not only an actual razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: like a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read רב חסדא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא was not limiting the rule to the tool itself. He meant the hair must be removed the way a razor removes it, right down to the skin. So any tool counts if it removes hair that cleanly.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, say (read the words differently)
like a razor, in the manner of a razor

phrases.english: Rather, say: like a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an actual razor cancels the days.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any tool counts if it removes hair the way a razor does, right down to the skin.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא: tearing or pulling out hair cancels the days only for most of the head, done like a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: a נזיר who tore out, plucked, or pulled out any amount of hair does not cancel his days unless it is most of his head, and like a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about tearing and plucking, which are not done with a razor, yet it still says 'with a razor.' That shows 'razor' here means the manner of removal, which fits the answer in step 7. It also confirms that most of the head is needed to cancel days.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (support from a ברייתא)
tore out (hair)
plucked
pulled out a little at a time

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
A נזיר who tore out, plucked,
or pulled out any amount [of hair]
does not cancel [his days] except
with most of his head, and with a razor.
phrases.notes: Tearing and plucking don't use a razor, so 'razor' here must mean 'done like a razor.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא as he was reread in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule: most of the head, done like a razor
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about tearing, plucking and pulling out hair

steps.title: רבי שמעון: two hairs are enough to cancel
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees: just as two leftover hairs ruin the final shaving, removing two hairs cancels the days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: just as two hairs hold back his shaving, so too two hairs cancel his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא records a different opinion, which says that removing just two hairs cancels the days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון compares the two laws. Two hairs are important enough to ruin the final shaving, so removing two hairs is important enough to cancel days. This argues with the first opinion, which requires most of the head.

keyTerms.meaning: just as
two hairs
cancel (the days)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון argues with the first opinion of the ברייתא, the view that רב חסדא follows. For him, two hairs, not most of the head, are enough to cancel the days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Just as two hairs hold him back,
phrases.notes: This refers to the final shaving, where two leftover hairs make it not count.

phrases.english: so too two hairs cancel [his days].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing two hairs cancels the נזיר's days, matching the two-hair amount of the final shaving.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on cancelling days: most of the head, done like a razor (רב חסדא and the first opinion of the ברייתא), or just two hairs (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: Three people whose shaving is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that a נזיר, a מצורע, and the לויים must shave. If they did not use a razor, or left two hairs, the shaving does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: three people shave, and their shaving is a מצוה: a נזיר, a מצורע, and the לויים. And all of them, if they shaved without a razor or left two hairs, have done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה from another place. It is setting up the next discussion, which will analyze this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these three, shaving is a required מצוה, not just something they are allowed to do. Here the משנה demands an actual razor and a full shave. Two leftover hairs make the whole shaving worthless, which matches רב חסדא's two-hair rule for the final shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned there (in a משנה elsewhere)
their shaving is a מצוה
a person with צרעת
the לויים, who shaved when they were first set apart for their service
they have done nothing at all

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נגעים.

phrases.english: Three shave, and their shaving is a מצוה:
a נזיר, a מצורע, and the לויים.
And all of them who shaved not with a razor,
or who left two hairs —
have done nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about shaving that is a מצוה. It prepares the next discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר, a מצורע and the לויים must shave as a מצוה. Shaving without a razor, or leaving two hairs, does not count.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say their shaving is a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the three people shave as a מצוה, and asks why it needs saying, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: three people shave, and their shaving is a מצוה. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה in Step 10 and asks why it needs to be said. The Torah already commands all three to shave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה commands a נזיר, a מצורע, and the לויים to shave. So calling it a מצוה seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to find what new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the way the גמרא quotes a source it just brought
Shaving
"It is obvious!": a challenge that a statement seems to teach nothing new

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 10.

phrases.english: Three people shave
and their shaving is a מצוה.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining the wording of the משנה quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words "their shaving is a מצוה"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה already commands all three to shave, so saying it is a מצוה seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Hair-removing paste does not count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's wording teaches that the point is the act of shaving, not just getting rid of hair. Using a hair-removing paste does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought the point is only to get rid of the hair, so even smearing on a hair-removing paste would be good enough. The משנה teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to say it. Without it, we might think any way of removing the hair would be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal were only to have no hair, a paste that dissolves hair would work. By calling it a מצוה of shaving, the משנה shows that the act of shaving itself is required.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have said": brings up a mistaken idea the source comes to rule out
Getting rid of hair
A paste that removes hair
"It teaches us": the new point the source is making

phrases.english: You might have said
that it is because of getting rid of the hair,
and so even if he smeared on a hair-removing paste, it works,
so it teaches us that it does not.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to rule out a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The aim is only to remove hair, so a hair-removing paste would be good enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצוה is the act of shaving, so a paste does not count.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 11.
steps.whatToRemember: Shaving as a מצוה means real shaving. Just removing the hair with a paste is not enough.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a מצורע must use a razor?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים say that a נזיר and the לויים shave with a razor. But what is the source that a מצורע must use a razor too?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches: if any of them shaved without a razor, it does not count. That makes sense for a נזיר, since it is written, "A razor shall not come upon his head." It also makes sense for the לויים, since it is written, "And let them pass a razor over all their flesh." But how do we know that a מצורע must use a razor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, that the shaving must be with a razor. It asks for the source for a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נזיר and for the לויים, the פסוק itself mentions a razor. For a מצורע, the תורה says to shave but does not mention a razor. So the גמרא needs some other source.

keyTerms.meaning: A razor
"Granted": this part is clear, before asking about the part that is not
A person with צרעת, who shaves as part of becoming pure
"From where do we know?": asks for a source

phrases.english: It teaches: and all of them
who shaved without a razor, it does not count.
Granted, about a nazir it is written:
"A razor shall not come upon his head."
And about the Levites it is written:
"And let them pass a razor over all their flesh."
But a metzora with a razor, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה from Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a מצורע's shaving must be done with a razor.

steps.title: Try to learn the מצורע from the לויים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests: the לויים must shave, and only with a razor, so a מצורע, who must also shave, should need a razor too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, let us learn it from the לויים: the לויים must shave, and their shaving must be with a razor. So too I will bring the מצורע, who must shave, and say his shaving must be with a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first try at a source, comparing the מצורע to the לויים. The words "if you say" warn us that a challenge is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is simple. Both the לויים and the מצורע are told to shave. Since the לויים must use a razor, the מצורע should have to use one as well.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you say": brings up an idea the גמרא is about to question
"Let it be learned from": learning one case from another
Requires, must have

phrases.english: And if you say, let it be learned from the Levites:
just as the Levites must shave,
and their shaving is only with a razor,
so too I will bring the metzora,
who must shave,
and say his shaving is only with a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare the מצורע to the לויים: both must shave, so both need a razor.

steps.title: The לויים are different: they were waved
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails. The לויים had something extra, their bodies were waved, and a מצורע does not have that.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: the לויים are special because their bodies had to be waved. Will you say the same about a מצורע, who does not have that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison to the לויים by pointing out a difference between them and a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לויים had a stricter process, since they themselves were waved like an offering. Maybe the razor rule comes with that stricter status. A מצורע is not waved, so we cannot be sure the razor rule carries over to him.

keyTerms.meaning: "It can be refuted": a difference that breaks a comparison
Waving, the motion done with certain offerings
"Will you say?": can you really apply it to the other case?

phrases.english: This can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִלְוִיִּם שֶׁכֵּן טְעוּנִין תְּנוּפָה בְּגוּפָם,
phrases.english: what about the Levites, who needed waving of their own bodies?
phrases.notes: The לויים themselves were waved like an offering (במדבר 8:11).

phrases.english: Will you say the same about a metzora, who does not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison offered in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the מצורע and the לויים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The לויים had something extra, being waved, which a מצורע lacks. So their razor rule may not apply to him.

steps.title: Try to learn the מצורע from the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the גמרא suggests learning the razor rule for a מצורע from a נזיר, who is not waved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let it be learned from a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second try. It compares the מצורע to a נזיר instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is not waved, so the problem from Step 15 does not apply. A נזיר also shaves with a razor, so he looks like a better match for the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather": moves to a new attempt after the last one failed

phrases.english: Rather, let it be learned from a nazir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 15 rejected the לויים, offers the נזיר instead.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare the מצורע to a נזיר, who shaves with a razor and is not waved.

steps.title: The נזיר is different: his offering has bread
steps.stepSummary: This comparison also fails. A נזיר's offering comes with bread, and a מצורע's does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a נזיר, whose offering needs bread? Will you say the same about a מצורע, who does not need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison to the נזיר by pointing out a different difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר has something extra, since his offering comes with loaves of bread. Maybe the razor rule comes with that. A מצורע's offering has no bread, so this comparison breaks down too.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering
Bread, here the loaves that come with the נזיר's offering

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְנָזִיר שֶׁכֵּן קׇרְבָּנוֹ טָעוּן לֶחֶם,
phrases.english: What about a nazir, whose offering needs bread?
Will you say the same about a metzora, who does not?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְנָזִיר שֶׁכֵּן קׇרְבָּנוֹ טָעוּן לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison offered in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the מצורע and the נזיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נזיר's offering needs bread and the מצורע's does not, so the razor rule may not carry over.

steps.title: Learn the מצורע from both cases together
steps.stepSummary: Neither case works alone, so the גמרא suggests learning the razor rule for a מצורע from the לויים and the נזיר together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it cannot be learned from one alone. Let it be learned from the two of them.
steps.whatsHappening: Each single comparison failed, so the גמרא puts the two cases together to teach about the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case had its own special feature: waving for the לויים, bread for the נזיר. But neither feature is shared by both, so neither can be the reason for the razor rule. What they do share is that both must shave and both need a razor, and the מצורע must shave too.

keyTerms.meaning: "It cannot be learned from one": one case alone is not enough
The two of them, both

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is going back to the failed comparisons. It is making a new argument, using what the two cases have in common, so that each one's special feature no longer matters.
steps.whatToRemember: A מצורע must shave with a razor. Neither the לויים nor the נזיר proves it alone, so the גמרא proposes learning it from both together.

phrases.english: Rather, it cannot be learned from one alone;
let it be learned from the two of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי מִתַּרְוֵיהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since Steps 15 and 17 each rejected a single source, joins the two sources together.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn the razor rule for a מצורע from the לויים and the נזיר together, based on what they share.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא learns a law: when each source alone has a weak spot, two sources together can prove it.

steps.title: The לויים alone cannot be the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which single case could teach the razor rule, and shows that the לויים fail because their bodies were waved.
steps.simpleTranslation: From which case can you learn it? If you learn it from the לויים, you can object: the לויים are special because their bodies had to be waved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lays out the earlier back-and-forth in its full, formal shape. It first shows that the לויים alone cannot teach the rule for a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule can only move from one case to another if the first case has nothing extra that could explain it. The לויים had the extra feature of תנופה of their bodies, so maybe that is why they needed a razor. A מצורע has no such waving.

keyTerms.meaning: From where can it come? Which source could teach it?
The לויים, who were shaved when they began their service
Waving of their bodies, a special part of how the לויים were set apart
What about X? X is special, because... (a standard way to reject a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. The גמרא is writing out steps 14–18 in their full formal shape so it can build the הצד השוה.

phrases.english: From which case can it be derived?
Let it be derived from the Levites,
[but] what about the Levites? They are special, since
they require waving of their bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהֵי תֵּיתֵי? תֵּיתֵי מִלְּוִיִּם, מָה לִלְוִיִּם שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out formally the proof from both cases that step 18 suggested.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the razor rule from the לויים alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The לויים have an extra feature, waving of the body, that a מצורע lacks.

steps.title: The נזיר shows waving is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר is not waved and still uses a razor, so waving cannot be what causes the razor rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נזיר will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection about waving by pointing to the נזיר. He is not waved, yet he also shaves with a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the razor rule came from waving, a נזיר would not need a razor. He does need one, so waving is not the cause. The objection against the לויים is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove: this case shows the objection does not matter
A person who took a vow of נזירות and shaves at its end

phrases.english: The nazirite will prove [otherwise],
phrases.notes: He means: a נזיר is not waved, yet he still shaves with a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection about waving raised in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נזיר is not waved but uses a razor, so waving is not the deciding factor.

steps.title: The נזיר alone cannot be the source either
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר's offering comes with bread, so maybe that extra feature is why he needs a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the נזיר? He is special, because his offering comes with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning from the נזיר alone, since he has his own extra feature: bread with his offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the waving of the לויים, the bread of the נזיר could be what causes the razor rule. A מצורע's offering has no bread, so the נזיר alone cannot teach the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: His offering
Requires bread to come along with it

phrases.english: What about a nazirite? He is special, since
his offering requires bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְנָזִיר שֶׁכֵּן קׇרְבָּנוֹ טָעוּן לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the נזיר brought in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the razor rule from the נזיר alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נזיר's offering needs bread, and a מצורע's offering does not.

steps.title: The לויים show bread is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The לויים had no bread with their offering and still used a razor, so bread cannot be the cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לויים will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the bread objection by going back to the לויים. They had no bread offering, yet they shaved with a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case now cancels the other's special feature. Waving is not the reason, because of the נזיר. Bread is not the reason, because of the לויים.

keyTerms.meaning: They will prove (plural form of יוֹכִיחַ)

phrases.english: The Levites will prove [otherwise].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bread objection from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לויים had no bread but used a razor, so bread is not the deciding factor.

steps.title: The shared feature teaches the razor rule for a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: Each case has its own special feature, but what they share is shaving with a razor, so a מצורע, who shaves, also needs a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has gone in a circle. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they have in common is that both must shave, and they shave with a razor. So I will add the מצורע: he must shave, and he shaves with a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof using a הצד השוה. It takes only the feature both cases share and applies it to the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither special feature (waving or bread) is found in both cases, so neither one can be the reason for the razor. The only thing left that both share is the need to shave. The מצורע also must shave, so he gets the razor rule too.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has returned to its starting point
The feature of this case is not like the feature of that case
The common factor shared by two cases
Shaving
A razor
A person with צרעת who shaves as part of becoming pure

steps.whatToRemember: A הצד השוה works like this: two cases, each with its own special feature, share one rule. Since neither special feature is in both, the shared rule must come from what they share, and it carries over to a third case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic model of a הצד השוה, a way of learning a rule that appears all over the תלמוד.

phrases.english: And the argument has gone back [to the start],
the aspect of this is not like the aspect of that,
and the aspect of that is not like the aspect of this.
The common factor between them
is that they require shaving,
and their shaving is with a razor.
So I too will bring the leper,
who requires shaving,
and [say] his shaving is with a razor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the circle of steps 19–22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מצורע must shave with a תער, learned through a הצד השוה from the לויים and the נזיר.

steps.title: רבא מברניש begins to attack the shared feature
steps.stepSummary: רבא מברניש tells רב אשי that the הצד השוה itself could be refuted, because the two cases share another special feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מברניש said to רב אשי: Let us refute it. What about the common factor between them? It is special, because...
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רבא מברניש wants to show that the לויים and the נזיר share something more than shaving, which a מצורע might lack. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה can be broken if the two source cases share another special feature besides the rule being learned. If they do, that shared feature might be the real reason for the razor. The specific feature comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us refute it, challenging the proof
רבא from the town of ברניש
A leading אמורא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rava of Barnish said to Rav Ashi,
But let us refute [it]:
What about the common factor between them? It is special, since
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the extra shared feature is named.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי, וְלִיפְרוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הצד השוה concluded in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה from the לויים and the נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two cases share another special feature that a מצורע lacks, that feature might be the real reason for the razor, so the proof falls apart.
